# The inner-being narrative — index and status (v1)

**Date:** 2026-09-30 · **Author:** Claude Code (draft for the researcher) · **Status:** first reset, built from the M47 inner-seat reading. Every chapter is a **draft for researcher review**. Nothing has been written to the DB.
**This file is a working index.** It may use project terms. The chapter files may not.

index_notes.heading: Researcher direction (verbatim, 2026-09-30)
index_notes.text: > "a) I expect many of the original claims to be affected. The original work in many respects were shallow, unfounded, incomplete. This must not be brushed over, each unfounded claim must be checked and restated. b) It is expected that the original work will be expanded and re-organised to align with the new research. to original must adjust to the new, not visa versa. c) the central theme has changed: originally the theme was around to two / three part structure; new theme is the inner being in operation described through the voice of the bible (per the prose.programme description of the project) d) the narrative is not a description of the history and pathway of the study, it articulates the findings and observation for what it is and depicted by scripture for a general reading without reference to the project terminology of clusters, phases, or other project specific terminology. Voice is first person, personal, direct, easy to read. Science chapters will be done later. Re-organised complete should encapsulate individual files, if there are individual files missing then I must dig for it. Holy Spirit study is separate - although many aspects of the Holy Spirit is an integral part of this study. The first step is to use the M47 result to reset the original study and do the relevant updates. Each next stream of work will add further updates to the narrative. Keep the core themes of the study in separate files (almost like chapters) but recognise it will untimately be combined into a single work."

index_notes.heading: Theme and frame
index_notes.text:
- **Central question:** how does the inner being work, as Scripture itself describes it?
- **Source:** the programme's own governing question, `prose_section` 128 (`prog_purp_observations_framework`): *"What are the inner workings of the human being as described in Scripture — characterising and grouping the inner characteristics, mapping their interrelationships, describing the spirit-soul-body boundary, and documenting the relational interfaces with God, other humans, and other spiritual beings?"*
- **Definition of the inner being:** section 5, `prog_purp_defining_inner_being`.
- **Audience:** section 7 — *"teachers, practitioners, thoughtful readers"*.
- **Title:** ***Inner Being in Operation***. Confirmed by the researcher on 2026-09-30: "approve 1916, title is Inner Being in Operation" (#1916).

index_notes.heading: Chapters (reading order)
index_notes.text:
**Companion working files** (in the parent folder):
- `../wa-essay-spirit-soul-body-claim-register-v48-20261012.md` — every original claim, with its verdict and restatement.
- `../wa-essay-spirit-soul-body-digest-v1-20260930.md` — the first digest.

index_notes.heading: Rules applied to the chapter text
index_notes.text:
- **No project terms:** no cluster, M-code, batch, stream, tag, Strong's number, phase, or "the study found".
- **Hebrew and Greek words** always appear with their gloss.
- **First person, direct, plain.** No account of how the study unfolded.
- **Quotations are ESV**, taken from verses read in the M47 files. A handful of well-known verses not quoted in those files are marked in the checks below.
- **Claude's readings** are written as the narrator's reading ("I read this as…"). No invented certainty.
- **Let Scripture speak for itself (researcher, verbatim, 2026-10-01):** *"you are bordering on imputing meaning that is not supported by the verses. don't drive synergy and phantom observations into the findings. Rather allow scripture to speak for itself."* A reading may restate what a verse or passage says. It may **not** join verses into a pattern, mechanism, division of labour or "what this shows" that no verse states. It may not use "most", "clearest" or "most often" unless it has been counted. When in doubt, quote and stop. Applied on 2026-10-01: 34 removals in the #1919/#1920 weaves (claim register v4), then 88 edits in the earlier passes (`../wa-essay-narrative-imputed-readings-audit-v1-20261001.md`, #1921). **Authoritative guide:** `Workflow/Instructions/wa-inner-being-narrative-style-guide-v2-20261001.md`.
- **Format (researcher, verbatim, 2026-10-01, #1924):** *"prose supported by bullets to handle different applications of the prose intro"*. Titles name the subject only, with no characterising subtitle. In the researcher's words, the four removed subtitles were *"AI assumptions and wrong"*.
- **External parties (#1924):** if any external party comes into play in the verses, it is dealt with in relation to the specific phenomenon, each in its own terms, and not watered down. External parties include God, the Spirit, other spirits, angels, other people, and the physical world. Guide §7a.
- **Held material** sits at the foot of Chapters 12 and 14 under a clearly marked working note. It is not part of the narrative until it is checked.

index_notes.heading: How later work updates this
index_notes.text:
**Weave, don't fit (researcher, verbatim, 2026-09-30, #1918):** *"There is a great danger of loosing important observations and impacts 'because it does not fit the current narrative.' Adding additional items is not a process of where does the new item support the current narrative - this is the wrong way around - it must be wove the new item into the narrative - knowing there is more to come."* So "does not fit" is never a reason to leave out an observation. When a new item does not fit, it is the narrative's structure that changes. The method is set out in `../wa-essay-narrative-weave-method-and-ch10-structure-v1-20260930.md` (proposal, awaiting approval).

**Change of character (researcher, verbatim, 2026-10-01, #1919):** *"One of the key discoveries in the study is how the meaning or application of the same concept / word changes in different circumstances … It must be built upon, not be set aside."* Every strand records when and how each word or concept changes character, and why. That is woven in, never dropped because another face of the same word is already in the text. Proposal: `../../../cross-cluster-web/origin-of-thought/origin-of-thought-change-of-character-v1-20261001.md` (**approved** 2026-10-01: "approve 1 2 3 4"). Built for the thought strand on 2026-10-01: ledger v2 §I. **Ch 11 §4 is the cross-cutting account and stays open.** Each operation file carries its own "when this changes character" passage.

- A later strand (e.g. fear, anger, doubt, the hands, thought) is **woven** through the chapters it touches, and it may reshape them.
- Each update is a **version bump** of that chapter file (`-v2-{date}`); the prior version goes to `archive/`.
- The **claim register** is updated in the same pass.
- New themes get new chapter files. This index records which strand fed which version.
- When the work is ready to become one book, the files are combined in reading order.

claims.original_wording: The soul goes to Sheol (Psa 16:10; 30:3; 49:15; 86:13; 89:48), so soul and spirit have different destinations

claims.claim_text: Most "spirit of …" phrases name a disposition that comes upon a person; the verse does not name a being. The same phrasing is used for good gifts: a spirit of wisdom, skill, grace, justice. Some are given by God: "the Lord has poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep" (Isa 29:10); the harmful spirit "from the Lord" (1Sa 16:14); God "sent an evil spirit" (Judg 9:23); the Lord "put a lying spirit" in the prophets' mouths (1Ki 22:23). 2Ti 1:7 says "God gave us a spirit not of fear". Spirit-beings are real (unclean spirits cast out; the spirit of divination, Act 16:16), but the one-to-one mapping to vice families is not in the text (SC; dep §2.3c; D §11.4)

Co-occurrence pulls: Q2, soul, spirit and breath with death words, 123 hits / 111 verses; Q3, heart with death words, 23 hits / 21 verses. Supplement §H: Luk 23:42–43; Phili 1:21–24; 2Cor 5:6–9.
- **Instruction:** the researcher, verbatim: *"prepare 1950 for approval and then adding it to the narrative"* (#1950 set ready for approval; woven with all four §F decisions as recommended).

**Original claims touched:**

| # | Before (verdict) | Evidence now read | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-9 | Soul to Sheol, so different destinations: **Restated** | Count of soul-delivered verses: 12 of 15 rescue from dying; Psa 49:15 and 16:10 look beyond death; Psa 89:48 none can | **Restated** (verdict unchanged); the restatement's wording corrected in place |
| 6-2 | Survival after death: **Restated** | Psa 49:15 ("he will receive me") and 49:19 ("his soul will go to the generation of his fathers"); Luk 23:43; Phili 1:23; 2Cor 5:8; 1Pe 4:6 | No change of verdict; more witnesses, set side by side |

**The narrative's own statements this change made:**

| Where | Before | After | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ch 2 "The inner person dying" → **"Soul, spirit and heart at death"** | "At death, Scripture gives each inner word its own verb", with one verb per word (the soul departs) | The soul departs, **dies** (Num 23:10; Judg 16:30, literally *let my soul die*; Eze 18:4), is **poured out** (Isa 53:12; Mat 26:38), is named to the end (Num 19:11), has **two ends beyond death** in Psalm 49 (49:10, 15, 19), and is not abandoned (Psa 16:10 with Act 2:31). The spirit is committed and returns; the body without it is dead; "who knows" (Ecc 3:21, moved here). "No verse sends the soul one way and the spirit another." The heart is named "while they live" (Ecc 9:3), and "I have found no verse that speaks of the heart after death." One reading marked "I read" | **Restated** (one verb per word was too narrow); NS |
| Ch 2 "Delivered from death" | "almost always about a living person rescued from dying" (uncounted); Psa 16:10 in the list | "most of them": 12 of 15, with 2 beyond death and 1 none can; Psa 16:10 moved | **Restated** (uncounted superlative) |

  - before it (Est 5:9; 2Ch 26:16, where the Hebrew has the heart lifted up)
  - where it is kept and planned (Job 36:13; Pro 6:14; Gen 27:41)
  - where it is taken to counsel (Neh 5:7, where the Hebrew is "my heart took counsel")

  - misreading another's heart (1Sa 17:28)

- **Ch 5, "Loving and hating one's own soul": Restated.** Ch 5 v3 called Job 10:1, Ecc 2:17 and Jon 4:3 "exhaustion rather than discipleship". **Researcher, verbatim:** *"yes M02, proceed with M47 first. I want to stress how important the reading back of clusters already narrated are. # Narrative audit — imputed readings removed (v1)

**Date:** 2026-10-01 · **Author:** Claude Code · **Escalation:** #1921 · **Status:** applied in place (in-review edits), for the researcher to review.
**Researcher, verbatim (2026-10-01):** *"you are bordering on imputing meaning that is not supported by the verses. don't drive synergy and phantom observations into the findings. Rather allow scripture to speak for itself."* Then: *"proceed with the #1921 audit of earlier readings."*
**Standard applied:** `Workflow/Instructions/wa-inner-being-narrative-style-guide-v1-20261001.md` §1, §2 and §8.2.
**Scope:**
- every chapter file, 01–15, read in full and checked for narrator readings and joining sentences
- every "I read / I take / I find", every "so" or "this shows", every superlative and frequency word
- this covers readings from the earlier passes (#1912–#1918); the 34 removals from today's weaves are listed separately in claim register v4
**Method:** a sentence was kept if a cited verse says it. It was cut back to the verses if it joined them into something no verse states, or if it used a count that was never made. Counted claims were kept, after the counts were checked:
- "the one word Scripture leans on most" (heart, about 930 verse rows against about 770 for soul; M47 stocktake §2)
- "about one verse in ten" (seat coverage)
- "life and myself … more often than soul" (Ch 4)

**Totals:** 88 edits.

updates.notes:
## 4. What the latest findings add that the original never had

These areas are absent from the original, or are listed there only as gaps. [Claude reading]

1. **Flesh as a full component** (original gap 1–2): kin, "all flesh", frailty, response to the inner seat, the "heart of flesh", and Paul's flesh as an orientation. Depiction §2.4; C §11.5; D §11.8; G §7.
2. **The heart as the centre**: inner speech ("said in his heart"), attention as "setting the heart", the heart as store, surface and soil, its opacity to all but God. Depiction §2.1; B §9.1; C §11.2.
3. **Conscience and bosom** (original gap 4): conscience as the NT's name for what the OT does with the heart ("David's heart struck him"); the bosom as the holding place. Depiction §2.5–2.6; D §11.6.
4. **The inner seat between persons**: souls knit, hearts stolen, spirit passed on, states spreading from one person to another. Depiction §3.8; F §14.
5. **The seat acted upon**: God turns, stirs, hardens and fills; the king's heart. H §7.1; G §11.
6. **The seat in motion** (the twelve threads, framework overview §5): thresholds of eating and drinking, components giving way in sequence, one word with opposite values, voices to the soul, the governed seat, hearing as the way in, spirits that arrive, wind and breath as emptiness, God's own heart and soul.
7. **Beyond the seat**: only about 10% of inner-being verses name a seat at all; twelve other ways the text carries an inner operation. Framework overview §6.
